questions.q: What makes an object a "standard object"?
options: It ships with every Salesforce org, built by Salesforce
It has more fields than a custom object
It cannot have any custom fields added to it
It only appears in Salesforce Classic
questions.explain: Standard objects like Account, Contact, and Lead ship with every org. Custom objects are the ones an admin builds for a specific org.

questions.q: A spreadsheet of property listings is moved into Salesforce as a Property object. What do the spreadsheet's column headers become?
options: Records
Reports
Fields
Page layouts
questions.explain: Column headers like Price or Bedrooms map onto fields on the object; each spreadsheet row becomes a record of that object.

questions.q: What distinguishes a Task from an Event?
options: A Task has a due date; an Event has a start and end time
A Task can never be marked complete
An Event can only be created by an admin
A Task is only visible to the record owner
questions.explain: A Task is a to-do with a single due date. An Event is scheduled time, with both a start and an end date/time.

questions.q: Is Contacts to Multiple Accounts enabled by default in a new Salesforce org?
options: Yes, it's on for every org automatically
It only applies to Person Accounts
No, it's an optional feature an admin turns on
It replaces the standard Contact object entirely
questions.explain: Contacts to Multiple Accounts is off by default — an admin has to enable it for indirect Account relationships to appear.

questions.q: Besides field-level settings, what else can you edit from Object Manager's own list?
options: Nothing — Object Manager's list is read-only
Only the org's overall security settings
Object-level settings, such as its label and description, via the row's Edit command
The Salesforce release version
questions.explain: Each row in Object Manager's list has its own Edit command for object-level settings, separate from the field-level settings inside the object.

questions.q: Why would an admin build a custom object like Energy Audit?
options: Because custom objects run faster than standard objects
Because standard objects cannot hold any records
Because no standard object represents that specific kind of data
Because custom objects don't require fields
questions.explain: Custom objects exist to cover data that no standard object (Account, Contact, Lead, etc.) represents.

questions.q: What does a Product (Product2) record represent?
options: The thing being sold, defined once and reusable across deals
A single line item on one specific Opportunity only
A formal PDF sent to a customer
A price list
questions.explain: A Product is defined independently of any one deal and can be reused across as many Opportunities as needed.

questions.q: What is the three-click path to creating any new custom field?
options: Reports tab → New Report → Fields
Object Manager → the object → Fields & Relationships → New
Setup → Chatter → New Field
App Launcher → Fields
questions.explain: Every custom field starts the same way: Object Manager, into the object, into Fields & Relationships, then New.

questions.q: What settings does a Checkbox field require beyond choosing the type?
options: Length and Decimal Places, same as Number
A list of values, same as Picklist
None — Checkbox is a simple True/False value with no length or precision to configure
A Related To object
questions.explain: Checkbox is the simplest field type: a single True/False value with no additional settings.

questions.q: Which two properties does this lesson say commonly work together on the same field?
options: Required and Picklist
Unique and External ID
Formula and Roll-Up Summary
Master-Detail and Checkbox
questions.explain: A field is very often marked both Unique (no duplicate key collides) and External ID (the field an integration matches on) at the same time.

questions.q: Why does Step 1 of the New Custom Field wizard offer the entire Data Type menu?
options: Because custom fields can change type after creation anyway
Because nothing about a field that doesn't exist yet is locked in
Because standard fields don't have a Data Type setting
It's a bug — only three types should show
questions.explain: A brand-new custom field hasn't been saved yet, so every data type family is still an open choice on Step 1.

questions.q: What is the core difference between a Text field and a Picklist field?
options: A Picklist restricts input to an admin-defined list of values; Text accepts anything typed
A Picklist can only hold numbers
A Text field is always required; a Picklist never is
There is no real difference
questions.explain: A Picklist only accepts values from a defined list, while a Text field accepts any typed input up to its length limit.

questions.q: What does the Insert Field tool in the formula editor let you do that's notable?
options: Only insert fields from the current object, never a related one
Insert a field reference, including fields on a related object reached across a relationship
Insert an image into the formula
Automatically fix syntax errors
questions.explain: Insert Field's picker can drill into a related object (like Account from an Opportunity), inserting correct cross-object syntax automatically.

questions.q: In the lesson's real example, what two different roll-up fields were built from the exact same two Product records?
options: Two COUNT fields with different filters
A SUM (Total List Price) and a MIN (Minimum List Price)
Two SUM fields on different objects
A Formula field and a Picklist field
questions.explain: The same two Product line items fed both a SUM roll-up (Total List Price) and a MIN roll-up (Minimum List Price) — same data, different aggregate, different answer.

questions.q: What is the key difference between Schema Builder and Object Manager, as described in this lesson?
options: Object Manager only works on custom objects, Schema Builder only on standard objects
They show completely unrelated information with no overlap
Schema Builder replaces Object Manager entirely and Object Manager is deprecated
Object Manager is where you create fields and relationships; Schema Builder is read-first, built for understanding structure
questions.explain: Object Manager is the edit-first tool for building fields and relationships; Schema Builder is read-first, designed to make the resulting structure easy to see at a glance.

questions.q: Which standard object is the only one that can use a Hierarchical Relationship field?
options: Account
Opportunity
User
Contact
questions.explain: Hierarchical Relationship is a special Lookup available only on the User object, typically used to build a management chain.

questions.q: What does one row on a junction object represent?
options: A duplicate of the parent record
Every possible pairing between the two related objects
A summary of all related records
A single pairing between one record on each side
questions.explain: Each junction record represents exactly one pairing — add ten related records and you get ten junction records, not ten new fields.

questions.q: Why does the Attendee side of the requirement need a junction object instead of a single relationship field?
options: Because junction objects are required for every relationship in Salesforce
Because Workshop is a custom object
Because it's a many-to-many relationship — an Attendee can register for many Workshops, and a Workshop has many Attendees
Because Contact cannot have any relationship fields
questions.explain: A single Master-Detail or Lookup field can only point to one parent, so modeling 'many on both sides' requires a junction object, as established in Lesson 17.

questions.q: Underneath the UI, what does a Lookup or Master-Detail relationship field actually store?
options: The related record's page layout
A formula that recalculates the relationship on every page load
A copy of the entire related record
A Salesforce ID pointing to the related record
questions.explain: Every relationship field covered in this chapter — Lookup, Master-Detail, junction — stores a Salesforce ID referencing the related record, not a copy of the record itself.

questions.q: Which relationship type does a Roll-Up Summary field require on the child object?
options: Master-Detail Relationship
External Lookup Relationship
Hierarchical Relationship
Lookup Relationship
questions.explain: Only Master-Detail gives Salesforce the structural guarantee needed to maintain a live aggregate, so Roll-Up Summary fields require it.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a Record Type?
options: To create a brand-new object
To permanently delete unused picklist values
To let a single object support multiple kinds of record, each with its own available picklist values and page layout
To rename a standard object
questions.explain: A Record Type lets one object represent more than one business process without creating a second object, by narrowing picklist values and assigning a page layout per Record Type.
